audits.resolution_reason: Unresolved parity-versus-color-membership teaching gap. 512 sampled frames cover only 3,4,7,8; independent rule mirrors diverge on color-9 witness. No actual Racket execution is claimed by this probe; require authority parity before a fix closes the finding.
audits.text:
## 79a14745b917

**Actionable teaching-distribution defect: generated frame colors do not identify parity.** The intended branch condition is odd versus even frame color, but normal generation chooses odd frames only from `{3, 7}` and even frames only from `{4, 8}`. Across 512 generated samples, the observed frame-color support was exactly `{3, 4, 7, 8}`. Therefore the lookup shortcut “flip left-right iff the frame color is 3 or 7; otherwise flip top-bottom” fits the complete sampled generator support without learning parity.

This shortcut fails on a lawful odd-color-9 frame: the intended rule flips its interior left-right, while the lookup shortcut flips it top-bottom. The saved evidence contains the exact input and both divergent outputs. This is especially relevant because color 9 is part of the canonical task domain. A minimal repair would rotate normal frame colors through all usable odd and even ARC colors, with schedule-level coverage ensuring each lesson cannot be explained by a fixed membership lookup.

Evidence: `checks/audit/79a14745b917/probe_palette_shortcut.py` and `checks/audit/79a14745b917/probe_output.json`, bound to generator SHA-256 `b44e19d1911acab73bfe063a0d9fafb2bc7d0b9c98361960455e8b3f29edb07b`.
